description: Server-side security: the local gateway's interception layer hijacks Host api.example.test, serving an attacker page without the backend's security headers while the real backend runs behind /internal in the same process and the proxy copy strips its headers. Remove the interception, restore the backend's exact X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options and Strict-Transport-Security values on the proxied and direct routes, keep the unknown-host 404, and write report/restore.md; the provided live gate tests/restore_test.py boots the gateway itself and asserts the restored behaviour.

criteria: The agent removed the interception layer (and the attacker page with its marker) from server/app.py and stopped dropping the backend's security headers, so Host api.example.test reaches the ExampleAPI backend on the proxied public routes and under /internal with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY and Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, and unknown hosts still get the proxy's 404.
python3 tests/restore_test.py passes, report/restore.md carries intercepted_host, stripped_headers_count = 3 and proxy_rule, and the gate, the incident note and the README are untouched.
